results.content: Your Trusted Legal Partner – Mylaw.id. # How to Register a Business in Indonesia: Legal Steps Every Entrepreneur Should Know. ### Starting a business in Indonesia is an exciting endeavor, but navigating the legal landscape can be overwhelming for first-time entrepreneurs. Whether you’re launching a small startup or opening a branch of an international company, it’s crucial to comply with local regulations from the very beginning. Here’s a step-by-step guide to legally registering a business in Indonesia:. Choose the Right Legal Entity**. The most common types of business entities in Indonesia are:. * **PT (Perseroan Terbatas)** – A limited liability company, suitable for local or foreign investors. * **CV (Commanditaire Vennootschap)** – A partnership firm, typically used for small-scale local businesses. Reserve Your Company Name and KBLI**. Your company name must be unique and approved by the Ministry of Law and Human Rights. KBLI, or Klasifikasi Baku Lapangan Usaha Indonesia, is the Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification. It’s a five-digit code used to categorize a company’s business activities. When registering a business, owners must specify the appropriate KBLI codes that accurately reflect their business operations. To decide on the correct KBLI, business owners should carefully review the detailed list of codes provided by the Indonesian Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) and select those that most closely match their intended business activities. It is crucial to choose the right codes as they impact licensing requirements and other legal aspects. results.title: The Importance and Benefits of BPJS for Expatriates in Indonesia
results.content: # The Importance and Benefits of BPJS for Expatriates in Indonesia. **Its Importance and Benefits for Expatriates**. BPJS (Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Sosial) has become a critical topic, especially for expatriates living in Indonesia. While many expatriates may initially overlook the personal benefits of this scheme, BPJS is now a legal requirement for all residents of Indonesia, including expatriates who have lived in the country for at least six months. Without compliance with BPJS payments, expatriates holding a KITAS will not be able to renew their residence permits. **What is BPJS and Who is Required to Register ?**. BPJS is a government program aimed at providing universal social security for all Indonesian citizens. The program covers health insurance, pension plans, work accident compensation, and death benefits. With BPJS, a basic standard of living can be maintained when participants’ income is reduced or lost due to workplace injury, old age, retirement, or death. **BPJS is divided into two main categories :**. 1. **BPJS Kesehatan (Health Insurance)**. Mandatory for every individual residing in Indonesia, BPJS Kesehatan offers health protection tailored to various needs. 2. **BPJS Ketenagakerjaan (Employment Social Security)**. Employers are required to register all their employees under this program. It provides protection against old age, workplace accidents, death, and retirement. If you work as a freelancer, you can register as an independent member under BPJS Mandiri Jamsostek. The BPJS program offers a range of crucial benefits, including :. * **Old Age Protection:** Ensures income during retirement. * **Workplace Accident Protection:** Provides compensation in case of work-related injuries. * **Death Benefits:** Offers compensation for the family of the deceased. * **Retirement Protection:** Provides financial support after retirement. Both employers and employees are required to contribute to the monthly BPJS payments. It’s important to note that BPJS is not a comprehensive health insurance package. If you require more specific healthcare coverage, you may need to consider additional health insurance. **Entrust Your BPJS Registration to Harmony**.
